brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro wrap (Reid). Brent crude closed below $100/bbl for the first time in two weeks after UNGA headlines suggested a narrowing US-Iran gap: a Kyodo report said Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US lifted its blockade, and Iran's FM Araghchi listed narrower reopening conditions than Iran's earlier demands (which also included sanctions relief and reparations), suggesting Iran may accept a narrower deal. Oil pared the decline after Trump's UN speech defended the Iran war, then fell again on 'very productive' US-Iran talks; Saudi Arabia separately aims for a partial East-West pipeline restart by Saturday. Equities were flat overall but diverged: the Nasdaq hit a fresh high on chip strength while financials fell on concerns AI could erode margins. The 2yr Treasury yield hit a two-year high as markets priced 75bps more Fed hikes by next June. The Franco-German spread neared its post-Euro-crisis high as Bundesbank's Nagel flagged a possible move to 'mild restrictive' ECB policy. Weaker Australian PMIs reinforced expectations for an RBA hike next week.
